text: Throughout the Spring Term, I consulted with Professor Andrew Leahy (my mentor) a few times regarding my Richter Research this summer. Our meetings, although short, gave me a clearer sense about my project and what I want to achieve by the end of the research period. However, we identified some concerns regarding the background knowledge needed for undertaking this research. The Murphy books are graduate level content, and so, they presume the readers have sufficient mathematical knowledge. Although I have taken many relevant courses at Knox, Professor Leahy still recommended me to go through some Calculus 3 and Mathematical Statistics content.

For Calculus 3, he provided a link to an online textbook. He told me to go through Chapter 5 (Multiple Integration), which is an important concept to understand how optimization in diffusion models works. He also advised me to complete some of the practice problems. During the Spring Term, I was able to go through some of the sections in the chapter, but due to the courseload, I wasn't able to do the practice problems. I plan on doing these once my finals finish and before my project starts on the 9th of June. Similarly, for Mathematical Statistics, I searched online for some videos covering topics like Random Variables, Normal Distributions and Probability Distributions. Again, I wasn't able to go too in-depth due to the course load during the term. After finals, I will consult with my mentor to see what I can go through to prepare myself for the graduate level readings.

Through my discussions with my mentor, we came to the conclusion that there is little to change regarding the initial timeline mentioned in my proposal. However, I might have to devote some additional time in the beginning weeks to make sure I have the required knowledge from Calculus 3 and Mathematical Statistics. The main objective of my project is to get a thorough understanding of the underlying mathematics in probabilistic generative models and its fine tuning techniques like LoRA. However, if time permits, I want to be able to use this theoretical knowledge and apply it in practice by doing hands-on implementations on fine-tuning such models. I plan to discuss this further with my mentor to fully understand how this can be achieved.
I have no particular questions I would like to ask currently.
